title: Open Problems on Laplacian Algorithms for General Integer-Weighted Graphs

source.title: 10-ish problems on Laplacian solving related things on general, integer weighted graphs

scopeNotes: The seed statements were supplied as a compact research agenda. Unless a record says otherwise, graphs may be sparse or dense, edge weights are positive integers represented in binary, n is the number of vertices, m is the number of edges or nonzeros, and U bounds the absolute input entries. Running-time goals are in bit operations when precision or exactness matters. The word 'faster' is sharpened relative to the cited primary-source baselines; where the seed milestone has already been achieved, the record explicitly identifies the remaining input-linear, output-sensitive, or optimal-sparsity question.

problems.sourceStatement: Faster solver for undirected Laplacians, vector error.
problems.problem: Obtain an input-optimal normwise solver for undirected integer-weighted Laplacian systems.
problems.wordDescription:
Undirected Laplacian systems can already be solved in expected time linear in the number of edges up to iterated-logarithmic factors, with logarithmic dependence on the requested normwise accuracy. These solvers are foundational primitives for graph optimization, random walks, spectral clustering, and scientific computing. The remaining question is whether the residual overhead is inherent or whether a solver can match the time needed to read the graph and write the solution.

The bit model is important for integer-weighted graphs. A unit-cost arithmetic statement can hide precision growth, while a vector-error guarantee only asks for a normwise approximation and should not pay the much larger cost needed for coordinatewise relative accuracy. A satisfactory result should therefore separate graph-size overhead, input bit length, and accuracy dependence.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let G be a connected undirected graph with n vertices, m edges, and integer weights in [1,U], let L be its Laplacian, and let b be an integer vector with 1^T b=0. For x=L^\dagger b, compute x_tilde satisfying ||x_tilde-x||_L <= epsilon ||x||_L with constant success probability. Determine whether this can be done in O(m log(1/epsilon)) word operations for polynomially bounded U, or in input-linear bit complexity up to factors depending only polylogarithmically on log U and log(1/epsilon). More generally, determine the optimal dependence on m, n, log U, and epsilon, improving the current m (log log n)^{O(1)} log(1/epsilon) expected-time frontier.

problems.sourceStatement: Faster solver for directed polynomial-mixing-time Laplacians, vector error.
problems.problem: Match the fastest undirected normwise solvers for directed Laplacians whose random walks mix in polynomial time.
problems.wordDescription:
Nearly-linear directed Laplacian solvers are known, but their polylogarithmic overheads, reductions to Eulerian systems, and dependence on sparsification remain substantially more involved than in the undirected case. When the associated random walk has polynomial mixing time and the weights are polynomially bounded, conditioning is controlled enough that precision is not the main obstruction. This regime isolates the structural cost of directionality.

A faster solver would immediately improve algorithms for stationary distributions, PageRank, hitting and escape probabilities, and other Markov-chain quantities. It would also test whether recent smaller Eulerian sparsifiers can close the runtime gap with the best undirected solvers.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let L be the column Laplacian of a strongly connected directed graph with n vertices, m arcs, polynomially bounded positive integer weights, and polynomial mixing time. Given b in im(L) and epsilon in (0,1), compute x_tilde approximating L^\dagger b in a stated norm, such as the U_L-energy norm after Eulerian scaling, where U_L=(L+L^T)/2 in the Eulerian case. Seek expected time m (log log n)^{O(1)} log(1/epsilon), or ideally O(m log(1/epsilon)), including all reductions from the general strongly connected case. The guarantee must state the stationary scaling, norm, success probability, and bit precision explicitly.

problems.sourceStatement: Complexity of a directed Laplacian solver with arbitrary mixing time, perhaps even with exact entries.
problems.problem: Determine the bit complexity of solving arbitrary-mixing directed integer Laplacian systems, including exact rational solutions.
problems.wordDescription:
Directed graphs with extremely slow mixing can have exponentially small stationary probabilities and badly conditioned Laplacian systems even when every edge weight has a short integer representation. Approximate arithmetic-operation bounds can therefore obscure the true precision cost. Exact solutions are rational and may encode weighted arborescence counts, so both their output length and the cost of producing them must be measured.

This problem asks for an output-sensitive theory that remains meaningful without a polynomial mixing-time promise. A sharp answer could range from a nearly input-linear approximate solver whose bit complexity depends only on the actual output precision, to an exact algorithm matching the total bit length of the rational solution up to lower-order factors, or to reductions showing that such targets are impossible.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let L be the directed Laplacian of a strongly connected n-vertex, m-arc graph with positive integer weights at most U, and let b be an integer vector in im(L). With no bound on mixing time or condition number, determine the optimal bit complexity of (a) computing a normwise epsilon-approximation to L^\dagger b and (b) outputting the exact rational vector L^\dagger b under a fixed normalization. Bounds should be expressed in m, n, log U, the bit length of b, epsilon, and the output length. A principal target is an output-sensitive exact algorithm, for example near O_tilde(m+output bits), or a conditional lower bound separating directed Laplacians from undirected ones.

problems.sourceStatement: Faster entrywise solver for undirected Laplacians.
problems.problem: Give a nearly input-linear bit-complexity solver with entrywise relative error for grounded undirected Laplacians.
problems.wordDescription:
Energy-norm accuracy does not protect coordinates whose true values are exponentially smaller than the norm of the solution. Hitting probabilities, escape probabilities, Green's functions, and related random-walk quantities require the stronger guarantee that every nonzero coordinate is approximated multiplicatively. This changes the relevant complexity from arithmetic operations to bit operations.

Recent work gives an approximately m sqrt(n) bit-operation algorithm for one SDDM system with entrywise guarantees. The open challenge is to remove the sqrt(n) overhead, understand whether a fine-grained obstruction prevents this, and identify the correct dependence on input precision and failure probability.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let M be an invertible SDDM matrix obtained, for example, by grounding one vertex of a connected undirected integer-weighted Laplacian, with m nonzeros and entries bounded by U. For a nonnegative integer vector b and x=M^{-1}b, output x_tilde such that exp(-epsilon)x_i <= x_tilde_i <= exp(epsilon)x_i for every i with x_i>0, with probability at least 1-delta. Improve the current O_tilde(m sqrt(n) log^2(U epsilon^{-1} delta^{-1})) bit bound toward O_tilde(m polylog(U epsilon^{-1} delta^{-1})), or prove a matching conditional lower bound.

problems.sourceStatement: Entrywise solver for directed Laplacians (polynomial weights, do better than n direct solves).
problems.problem: Compute an entrywise approximate inverse of a polynomially weighted directed grounded Laplacian in near-output-linear time.
problems.wordDescription:
Computing all entries of a directed Laplacian inverse exposes all-pairs hitting, escape, and Green's-function information. Running a single-right-hand-side routine once per column ignores the shared graph structure and can be far more expensive than the n^2 values that must be written. The natural goal is an output-sensitive algorithm.

The original milestone of beating n unrelated direct solves has already seen substantial progress: 2025 algorithms for fixed-point row-diagonally-dominant L-matrices are subcubic in dense regimes and improve on straightforward repeated solving in important sparse regimes. The sharpened open problem is to reach n^{2+o(1)} bit operations for sparse polynomially weighted graphs, or otherwise characterize the optimal tradeoff among m, n, and matrix-multiplication exponents.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let M be an invertible RDDL matrix obtained by grounding a strongly connected directed Laplacian, with m nonzeros and integer entries bounded by U=n^{O(1)}. Output Z satisfying exp(-epsilon)(M^{-1})_{ij} <= Z_{ij} <= exp(epsilon)(M^{-1})_{ij} for all positive entries, with probability at least 1-delta. Seek O_tilde(n^2 + m n^{o(1)}) bit operations, or any bound that improves the current O_tilde(min{n^{omega+1/2}, m n^{3/2+o(1)}}) inversion frontier throughout a nontrivial parameter range. Determine matching lower bounds, noting that n^2 output entries are unavoidable.

problems.sourceStatement: Faster O(n)-sized sparsifier for undirected Laplacians.
problems.problem: Construct optimal-size undirected spectral sparsifiers in input-linear time.
problems.wordDescription:
For fixed accuracy, every undirected weighted graph has a spectral sparsifier with O(n) edges, and such a sparsifier can already be constructed in almost-linear randomized time. Thus the broad existence-and-almost-linear-time milestone in the seed statement has been achieved. The remaining problem is to remove residual runtime and accuracy overhead while retaining the optimal O(n/epsilon^2) edge count.

An input-linear algorithm would make optimal sparsification as cheap as reading the graph and would simplify many downstream solver and optimization pipelines. The deterministic version remains substantially harder: a very recent construction makes major progress for dense graphs, but retains polylogarithmic sparsity overhead and a roughly quadratic additive runtime term.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Given an undirected n-vertex, m-edge graph with positive integer weights and epsilon in (0,1), output a reweighted subgraph H with O(n/epsilon^2) edges satisfying (1-epsilon)L_G <= L_H <= (1+epsilon)L_G. Seek O(m) expected time for constant epsilon, or O(m polylog(1/epsilon)) time with explicit bit complexity, improving current O_tilde(m/epsilon^{O(1)}) constructions. Separately determine whether the same target is possible deterministically.

problems.sourceStatement: Smallest sized sparsifier for Eulerian sparsifiers.
problems.problem: Determine the optimal edge count of spectral sparsifiers for Eulerian directed Laplacians.
problems.wordDescription:
Eulerian directed sparsification must approximate an asymmetric Laplacian while preserving in-degree/out-degree balance. Undirected graphs admit the optimal O(n/epsilon^2) edge bound, but current Eulerian constructions retain polylogarithmic factors. Those factors propagate directly into the cost and complexity of directed Laplacian solvers.

The central structural question is whether directionality forces extra edges or whether the undirected optimum remains attainable. Both existential and efficient-construction versions matter: proving a smaller sparsifier exists may require discrepancy tools, while finding it in almost-linear time adds algorithmic constraints.
problems.mathematicalConditions: For an n-vertex weighted Eulerian directed graph with Laplacian L and U_L=(L+L^T)/2, determine the minimum s(n,epsilon) such that there is an Eulerian reweighted subgraph with s arcs whose Laplacian L_tilde is an epsilon-approximation to L in the standard asymmetric norm induced by U_L. Close the gap between the Omega(n/epsilon^2) lower bound inherited from undirected graphs and the best known O(n log^{3/2}(n)/epsilon^2) polynomial-time upper bound (up to alternative mixed epsilon terms). In particular, prove or refute s(n,epsilon)=Theta(n/epsilon^2), and seek an almost-linear-time construction if it holds.

problems.problem: Improve the update-query tradeoff for fully dynamic approximate effective resistance on general weighted graphs.
problems.wordDescription:
Effective resistance is a basic dynamic measure of connectivity and a central primitive behind sparsification, electrical-flow optimization, and random-walk analysis. Maintaining a spectral edge sparsifier is not by itself enough for fast arbitrary-pair resistance queries: evaluating a query still requires access to an inverse or a suitable dynamic Schur complement.

Existing general-graph data structures achieve sublinear but polynomial update and query bounds, with different guarantees for unweighted versus weighted graphs and for oblivious versus adaptive adversaries. The open goal is to lower these exponents, obtain worst-case rather than amortized bounds, and understand which combinations are ruled out by dynamic lower bounds.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Maintain an undirected graph with positive integer conductances under edge insertions, deletions, and weight changes. On a query (s,t), return R_eff^G(s,t) within a factor 1+epsilon. Improve the best general-graph tradeoffs, including the O_tilde(n^{2/3+o(1)} epsilon^{-O(1)}) amortized scale for all-pairs queries, while supporting polynomially bounded weights. Desired results include update and query times n^{1/2+o(1)} or better, worst-case guarantees, and robustness to an adaptive adversary; alternatively prove conditional lower bounds that identify the optimal frontier.

problems.sourceStatement: Dynamic electrical flows with heavy hitters (find all edges whose electrical flow values are greater than epsilon of the total).
problems.problem: Maintain an output-sensitive heavy-hitter oracle for electrical flows under dynamic resistances and demands.
problems.wordDescription:
Optimization algorithms based on electrical flows often need only the few edges carrying a large fraction of the current flow or energy. Recomputing the full m-dimensional electrical flow after every resistance or demand update defeats this sparsity. A dynamic heavy-hitter oracle would expose the important coordinates without materializing the entire flow.

Specialized versions of this idea already power faster maximum-flow algorithms, but they rely on restricted update sequences and amortization tailored to an interior-point method. The broader open problem is to build a reusable data structure for general dynamic graphs, with a clean approximation guarantee and update/query bounds that scale with the number of reported heavy edges.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let G have incidence matrix B, resistance matrix R, Laplacian L=B R^{-1} B^T, and dynamic zero-sum demand b. The electrical flow is f=R^{-1}B^T L^\dagger b and its energy is E=f^T R f. Support resistance updates, edge insertions/deletions, and sparse changes to b. A query with epsilon must output a set H containing every edge e with sqrt(r_e)|f_e| >= epsilon sqrt(E), excluding every edge below (epsilon/2)sqrt(E), together with constant-factor or 1+o(1) estimates of reported values. Seek sublinear, ideally polylogarithmic, amortized update time and O_tilde(epsilon^{-2}+|H|) query time, under a clearly stated adversary and numerical model.

problems.problem: Estimate an undirected Laplacian cofactor multiplicatively in nearly input-linear time.
problems.wordDescription:
By the matrix-tree theorem, a cofactor of an undirected graph Laplacian is the total weight of its spanning trees. Approximating the log determinant additively can be done in near-linear time, but that guarantee may correspond to a very large multiplicative error in the determinant itself. A genuine 1+epsilon estimate of the determinant is therefore a stronger counting problem.

Recent work gives a roughly m^{3/2}/epsilon-time multiplicative estimator by repeatedly removing uncorrelated edge sets, improving earlier sparse-graph bounds. Closing the remaining gap to near-linear time would connect electrical-flow localization, determinant-preserving sparsification, and high-accuracy trace estimation in a particularly clean setting.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Given a connected undirected graph G with n vertices, m edges, and positive integer weights at most U, fix a root r and let tau(G)=det(L_{-r,-r}), the weighted spanning-tree count. With probability at least 1-delta, output tau_tilde satisfying (1-epsilon)tau(G) <= tau_tilde <= (1+epsilon)tau(G). Seek O_tilde(m poly(epsilon^{-1},log U,log delta^{-1})) bit operations, improving the known O_tilde(m^{3/2} epsilon^{-1}) sparse-graph bound and the earlier roughly n^2 epsilon^{-2} determinant-preserving bound. The result must distinguish multiplicative determinant error from additive error in log tau(G).

problems.problem: Develop a nearly input-linear multiplicative estimator for directed Laplacian cofactors and weighted arborescence counts.
problems.wordDescription:
A cofactor of a directed Laplacian counts rooted weighted arborescences. Unlike the undirected case, the matrix is asymmetric and current spectral sparsification controls a norm induced by the symmetrization rather than determinant directly. There is no immediate directed analogue of the determinant-preserving SDDM machinery.

A fast estimator would provide a counting counterpart to nearly-linear directed Laplacian solvers and could illuminate stationary-distribution normalization, since directed tree weights encode stationary masses. The problem is meaningful both for Eulerian graphs, where the spectral theory is cleanest, and for general strongly connected graphs.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Given a strongly connected directed graph with n vertices, m arcs, and positive integer weights at most U, fix a root r and let tau_r=det(L_{-r,-r}), the total weight of spanning in-arborescences rooted at r under the chosen Laplacian convention. Output a (1+epsilon)-multiplicative estimate with failure probability at most delta. Seek O_tilde(m poly(epsilon^{-1},log U,log delta^{-1})) bit operations first for Eulerian graphs and then for arbitrary strongly connected graphs. Establish whether directed spectral or singular-value sparsifiers preserve enough information for this purpose, or identify a different primitive.

problems.problem: Determine the exact bit complexity of Laplacian determinants and weighted spanning-tree or arborescence counts.
problems.wordDescription:
Generic exact algorithms compute the determinant of an integer matrix in essentially integer-matrix-multiplication time. A reduced graph Laplacian is much more structured: it is sparse, diagonally dominant in the undirected case, and its determinant is a positive combinatorial count. It is unknown how far this structure can reduce exact bit complexity on general graphs.

The problem should be treated as exact symbolic computation rather than numerical linear algebra. Any claimed speedup must account for coefficient growth, modular reconstruction, and the output length of the integer determinant. Directed and undirected Laplacians may have different algorithmic behavior even though both admit matrix-tree interpretations.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Given a connected undirected graph or strongly connected directed graph with n vertices, m edges or arcs, and positive integer weights at most U, compute exactly det(L_{-r,-r}) for a specified root r. Determine the optimal randomized and deterministic bit complexity as a function of m, n, and log U. Improve on applying generic integer determinant algorithms, whose dense Las Vegas complexity is (n^omega log U)^{1+o(1)}, by exploiting Laplacian sparsity and graph structure; an aspirational target is O_tilde(m+n^2) or another output-sensitive bound. Alternatively, establish reductions or conditional lower bounds showing that exact Laplacian determinant is as hard as a standard exact-linear-algebra primitive.
